                    ### Question
                    A patient presents to the clinic with symptoms of dizziness on standing up. He says it started soon after he was diagnosed with hypertension and started taking treatment for it. He has no other medical history. The physician decides to switch to another antihypertensive that does not cause orthostatic hypotension. Which of the following should be the drug of choice for this patient?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Enalapril
opb. Methyldopa
opc. Clonidine
opd. Amlodipine
ope. Propanolol

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
The patient presents with dizziness upon standing, indicative of orthostatic hypotension, likely caused by antihypertensive treatment. Amlodipine, a calcium channel blocker, is preferred as it is less likely to cause orthostatic hypotension compared to other options. Enalapril (an ACE inhibitor) and methyldopa can cause dizziness but are not primarily associated with orthostatic hypotension. Clonidine and propranolol can also lead to sedation and dizziness. Therefore, switching to Amlodipine is the most appropriate choice for managing hypertension without exacerbating orthostatic hypotension.
